A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REL benchmark study. All 32 pages in each version are readable, including matching figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E; no material comparison gaps were found.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original LLM evaluations across algebra, biology and chemistry. Appendices A and D contain further benchmark results, intervention experiments and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations in Section 5 and the additional results and analyses in Appendices A and D.

M1.justification: REL's task-generation and scoring procedures are unchanged, including the neighborhood-sum generator in Algorithm 1 and the epistasis-label construction in Appendix A.3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same algebra, homoplasy, epistasis and molecular reasoning tasks. Appendix coverage, including REL-B2's protein fitness datasets and REL-C4's motif-selection task, is unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated model sets remain unchanged: Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro Preview and GPT-5.2, alongside the same GPT-5.4 tool-assisted comparison and Llama 3.1-70B/Qwen3-4B evaluations in Tables A.6–A.7.

E3.justification: Sample counts, eight-choice algebra evaluation, homoplasy scoring, chemistry metrics and intervention settings are identical. Both versions report the same 4,096/8,192/16,384-token budgets and one-shot evaluation subsets.

E4.justification: The confounder analyses, operand-complexity manipulations, inference-time interventions, structured prompting, best-of-N/majority voting and qualitative failure analyses are retained without revision in Section 5 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Table A.6 retains means and standard errors across questions. Appendix D.6 still reports five GPT-5.2 runs per question for 15 questions at each of four RC levels; uncertainty displays and statistical procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix scores, trends and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Section 5.3 retains chemistry completion rates of 65.7%, 38.1% and 26.0% for REL-C1/C2/C3, and Table A.11 retains identical baseline and structured-prompting accuracies.

T1.justification: The RC/OC definitions in Section 3, neighborhood constraints in Appendix A.2, and epistatic-coefficient equations and classification thresholds in Appendix A.3.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same contributions and claims: REL controls relational complexity across three scientific domains, higher RC challenges current models, and the tested inference interventions do not eliminate this limitation.

C2.justification: The binding-bottleneck interpretation and Appendix D's failure explanations are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning multiple-choice evaluation, context-length constraints and synthetic tasks.

D1.justification: The front-page GitHub destination changes from ada-f/relational_reasoning to mims-harvard/rel-reasoning, and the Hugging Face dataset destination changes from ada-f/rel to mims-harvard/rel. These revise access instructions; implementation details, generation parameters and example prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B–C. Guha (2013) remains the same work; its revised publication details and added DOI are bibliographic metadata edits.

P1.justification: v2 adds the missing equal-contribution explanation, replaces the preprint notice with ICML/PMLR publication information, and updates the Guha reference entry. Scientific prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded first-page notes and small spacing changes produce limited column and page reflow. Figures and tables retain their content and design; all appendix pages render identically between versions.

improvement.justification: The authorship clarification, publication/reference updates and revised resource links are limited documentation changes. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, with no meaningful overall quality gain or loss established by the PDFs.
